last_amend_reason: ESC-013 approved class, tickets.json verify fields ONLY, 8 tickets. T-160 measured NINE closed tickets whose recorded verify passes identically with and without their defect - the mechanism by which each was closed without anything distinguishing the defect from its repair. T-160 own text named only three, and two thirds of that text is stale: T-109 self-repaired and T-111 does reach its grader. Eight are repointed here from whole-suite or non-attributing commands onto the specific graders that name them. T-000: make verify is the disjunction of 5600 tests and four tools, now three scaffold files, 35 passed. T-010: 14 files really do grade all six clauses but NONE names T-010 in its AST - the three Python mentions are comments, discarded by the anti-forgery rule, and the TS one is never collected; a lexical miss rather than a vacuous gate, now widened to include the files that do name it. T-111 and T-129 and T-118: verify.sh check, whole-suite, non-attributing. T-112 is the strongest true positive - test_schema_grants.py reads docker-compose.yml only to SCRAPE image and POSTGRES_ settings for a throwaway container and injects the password via docker run -e, so deleting the compose forwarding it supposedly grades leaves it at exit 0; now test_role_password_end_to_end.py, 20 passed. T-122: whole-suite plus lint and vitest; its own acceptance 1 IS the whole-repo run, which is why the gate could not single it out. T-123: the defect and repair live in scripts/bootstrap.sh while the operand was packages/llm, where git grep bootstrap returns exactly one hit, prose in an __init__ docstring - reverting the recursive-chflags repair left it at exit 0. WORKER SLOTS WERE NOT REWRITTEN: each new string carries its ticket own existing ${PROXYSHOP_GATE_WORKER:-N} token forward verbatim (5, 1, 11, 11, 11, 13, 2, 9), because writing a literal would have silently reverted amendment 22 for these eight rows and collapsed them back onto one Postgres database and one Redis logical DB. MEASURED AFTER THE EDIT: T-160 goes 9 violators to 1 and STAYS RED, so it does not XPASS and no strict-xfail marker has to be removed - which is exactly why the ninth is excluded. T-133 IS DELIBERATELY LEFT AS A VIOLATOR AND MUST NOT BE REPOINTED YET. Two of its three acceptance clauses are unmet at HEAD, which is why they have no grader: git grep publish_profile over tracked files returns its definition, its __all__ entry, and exactly ONE call site - apps/buyer/svc/tests/test_auth_vault.py:786, a test. The convenient reading, that the selector is wrong, was ruled out: the same grep finds read_profile in production at auth/routes.py. The ticket own objective says the root causes remain and open T-142 exists for it. Repointing would hand it an honest-looking gate over one third of its acceptance and make that permanent, because afterwards it reads as fully graded. It is being reopened on a rejected verdict instead. THREE CAVEATS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. (1) T-000 acceptance 1 is literally make verify exits 0, and the sweep treats make verify anywhere as whole-suite, so A1 becomes structurally ungradeable; the trio covers A2 well and A3 partially. (2) THE STRUCTURAL HOLE UNDER ALL OF THIS: gate_violations asks only selected AND owned, so a file whose every ticket-naming test SKIPS at runtime satisfies it identically to one where they all run. Three of these eight depend on it - T-112 only clause-3 graders carry a BARE @pytest.mark.docker so a Redis or Neo4j blip skips its only end-to-end evidence for datastores it never touches (one-token fix: @pytest.mark.docker("postgres")); T-123 clauses 3 and 5 rest on a test decorated skipif(shutil.which("chflags") is None), which skips on any non-macOS host; most of T-129 ingest graders are docker plus graph. Marker DESELECTION is a non-issue, exactly one deselection repo-wide grading neither ticket; runtime SKIPPING is the real exposure. (3) The gate accepts any collected file naming the ticket in its AST, so the decoy surface is the count of alternative graders: T-111, T-123 and T-133 have one each and are pinned exactly, T-122 has seven and T-000 twenty-one. Two were run and both are one-field tickets.json edits that satisfy T-160 while grading nothing. Closing that needs a rule the sweep does not have, such as a floor on selected non-skipped test count. TWO OPERANDS WERE REMOVED AFTER ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, both verified by reading source: T-122 two pkgroot_fallback tests name T-122 to record an EXEMPTION from its sweep - they are anti-graders and including them made the gate look three times stronger; and T-118 test_stub_permalink.py, whose sole T-118 token is a blast-radius control docstring. The neighbouring T-262 sweep is untouched, measured rather than reasoned: identical clause output before and after, T-087, T-228, T-130, T-134. Ratchets after this: closed-gated 59 against floor 57, not-yet-closed-gated 94 against floor 84.
